'''''Limonium binervosum''''', commonly known as '''rock sea-lavender''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is an [[wikt:aggregate species|aggregate species]] in the family [[Plumbaginaceae]].

Despite the common name, rock sea-lavender is not related to the [[lavender]]s or to [[rosemary]] but is a [[perennial]] [[herb]] with small violet-blue flowers with five petals in clusters.<ref>{{cite book | last = Barnes | first = Richard | title = Coasts and Estuaries | publisher = Hodder & Stoughton Ltd | year = 1979 | pages = 92–93 }}</ref>

Eight rock sea-lavenders are [[endemism|endemic]] to [[Great Britain|Britain]] and [[Guernsey]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web.guernsey.net/~cdavid/botany/files/limonium%20binervosum/index.html |title=Limonium binervosum, Rock Sea Lavender |accessdate=2008-05-03 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723141053/http://web.guernsey.net/~cdavid/botany/files/limonium%20binervosum/index.html |archivedate=2011-07-23 }} Guernsey web site accessed 2008-05-03</ref> and the taxonomy was reviewed in 1986 to include a range of subspecies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wirral.gov.uk/LGCL/100006/200029/745/content_0000643.html |title=Rock Sea-Lavender |accessdate=2008-05-03 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080607121553/http://www.wirral.gov.uk/LGCL/100006/200029/745/content_0000643.html |archivedate=2008-06-07 }} Wirral web site accessed 2008-05-03</ref>

Growing 10–70 cm tall from a [[rhizome]], ''Limonium binervosum'' flourishes in [[soil salinity|saline]] soils, so are therefore common near  the western [[coast]]s and in [[salt marsh]]es, and also on saline, [[gypsum]] and [[alkaline]] soils such as found on [[Flat Holm]] island in [[Wales]], [[UK]]
